input.quote: However, any Party may terminate its participation in this Agreement at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter by giving not less than one (1) year's prior notice thereof, in writing, to the other Parties.
input.rationale: Paragraph 18 locks every Party in for a 25-year Initial Period: 18.1 permits termination of participation only at the end of the Initial Period or thereafter, and 18.2 allows in-period termination only by unanimous written agreement of all Parties. Teleglobe therefore has no convenience exit at all during a multi-year committed term, which is walk-away territory and fails fallback elements 1 and 2. The counterparty-side elements are already satisfied by 18.1: the other Parties may exit only at or after the end of the Initial Period, and only on one year's notice (well above the 90-day floor), so we have left that sentence verbatim. We therefore target the fallback and add a single Teleglobe-only convenience right on 90 days' notice with any early-termination fee capped at three months' fees; a narrow "Notwithstanding Subparagraph 18.1" opener is needed because 18.1 otherwise fixes the timing of participation exits.

proposal.summary: Add a Teleglobe-only convenience exit on 90 days' notice with early-termination fees capped at three months' fees
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that we must be able to exit on notice without penalty, so we have added a Teleglobe-only convenience termination on ninety (90) days' notice with any early-termination fee capped at three (3) months' fees; we have left the other Parties' end-of-Initial-Period exit on one year's notice untouched.

ops.text: Notwithstanding Subparagraph 18.1, Teleglobe USA Inc. may terminate its participation in this Agreement for convenience at any time, including during the Initial Period, by giving not less than ninety (90) days' prior notice thereof, in writing, to the other Parties, and any early-termination fee payable by Teleglobe USA Inc. in respect of such termination shall not exceed three (3) months' fees.
